h.strategy: Favor hypotheses driven by strong structural mechanisms: (1) an edit matters less when the part it modifies is disconnected, bypassed, or redundant in the parent; (2) diminishing returns: adding capacity helps less when the parent already has plenty, and removing it hurts more when the parent has little; (3) bottlenecks: improving a component helps more when it is the sole path or limiting factor. Prefer conditions that change the edit's effect by a large amount over subtle ones. Avoid hypotheses whose direction depends on fine balances between competing effects. State each hypothesis's mechanism in one sentence.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input so upgrading edge 4 has no effect.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, edge 2 carries no signal to process.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv adds a whole direct path, a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
Replacing a removed edge with a conv adds capacity where there was none.
Restoring the bottleneck edge into the output with a conv unlocks the whole node 2 branch.
Replacing none with a conv opens a new learnable path from node 1 to the output.
Edge 0 gates all of node 1's paths, so restoring it with a conv enables them.
Removing edge 4 is harmless when node 1 is dead, but usually costly otherwise.
Edge 4 is dead when node 1 has no input, so the edit has nothing to act on.
Adding a direct conv path where none existed gives more gain than modifying an existing op.
